headline: Nvidia beat and guide ease AI fears; FOMC minutes and Anthropic pricing are next

what_happened.summary: The Cboe Daily Take 'Nvidia's Earnings and Guidance Soothe Investor Worries' (17 Nov) says Nvidia beat top- and bottom-line expectations and guided Q4 revenue to $130 billion against analysts' $125.3 billion. Nvidia and other AI and semiconductor names rose after hours. Cboe notes the gross margin forecast came in below Q3 and that open questions on succession remain for the call. The regular session was still weak: FRED shows the Nasdaq-100 closed at 27001.78 (-0.72%). The Daily Take says the S&P 500 fell 1.0% and the Nasdaq Composite 0.74%. Unverified headlines this morning describe futures rising on the Nvidia numbers; there are no live prices in the inputs, so this brief does not say where NQ trades.
what_happened.market_action: Per the Daily Take, 17 Nov was the fourth straight losing session for the Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500, and the Dow lost 1.6%. Cboe volatility indices rose again: VIX 25.46 (+11.13%), VXN 34.44 (+4.68%), VVIX 121.28, VIX9D 26.7 and COR1M 20.13 (+22.59%). The Daily Take text puts VIX at 23.56, which repeats the figure in the prior day's article, so the Cboe index table is used here. FRED's S&P 500 series only runs to 16 Nov (7416.59, -1.92%).
what_happened.macro: Treasury (primary source) shows yields lower on 17 Nov: 2-year 4.8% (-3.0 bp), 10-year 5.1% (-2.0 bp), 30-year 5.46%. The Daily Take says October retail sales rose 0.2% headline and 0.5% core. The unofficial consensus was 0.1% and 0.4%, so both were slightly above forecast. Cboe says the CME FedWatch probability of a 25 bps December hike rose to 97.4%. Polymarket shows 92.5% for a 25 bps hike and 5.0% for 50+ bps. HY OAS was 3.34 (+11 bp) as of 16 Nov, up from 3.23 on 13 Nov.
what_happened.geopolitics: The Daily Take says WTI rose moderately to the mid-$85 range after continued tanker attacks in the Middle East. Official FRED oil data are stale to 11 Nov (Brent 92.14, WTI 89.62). An unverified oil headline says crude fell on rising US inventories.
what_happened.company_news: An NVIDIA 8-K filed 17 Nov (primary source) confirms the quarterly results release, with CFO commentary from Colette Kress as Interim CEO. Cboe reports she said the Vera Rubin platform is 'off to an explosive start'. Cboe, citing the Wall Street Journal, says Anthropic's IPO could price above $80 per share when it finalises today, with first trading Thursday. An unverified headline says Waller may favour a half-point hike.

driver_reason: Nvidia's first report since the CEO resigned is the dominant catalyst. Cboe's Daily Take says the results and guidance lifted AI and semiconductor names after hours, after two sessions of AI-led selling. The Fed hike path (97.4% per Cboe's FedWatch citation) is the background risk, with the FOMC minutes due tonight.
leader_reason: Nasdaq-100 minus S&P 500 was -0.75 pct pts on 16 Nov and -0.78 over five sessions, and VXN minus VIX is 8.98 pts, so tech carries the extra risk premium. Engine read: on 17 Nov the Nasdaq-100 fell 0.72% while Cboe says the S&P 500 fell 1.0%, so the underperformance paused for a day, and rising COR1M (20.13) suggests the selloff is broadening.

overlap_with_previous.echo_check: The Fed hike theme is partly echo: odds barely moved, and the Waller item is a headline only. The Daily Take's VIX line (22% to 23.56) repeats the previous day's text and conflicts with the Cboe index data (25.46), so it is not new evidence. The Nvidia theme is not echo, since results and guidance are new primary evidence.

scenarios.name: bear
scenarios.text: The Nvidia relief fades (Cboe flags a lower gross margin forecast and unresolved succession questions) or the minutes read hawkish, and the Nasdaq-100 closes more than 1.3% lower.
scenarios.invalidation: A broad AI and semiconductor bid that holds through the session while yields stay lower.

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.text: A relief gain is offset by caution ahead of the minutes and the Anthropic debut, giving a move inside the 1.3% band.
scenarios.invalidation: A decisive move beyond 1.3% in either direction, for example a hawkish surprise from the minutes.

scenarios.name: bull
scenarios.text: The Nvidia beat and $130 billion guide revive the AI trade and the Nasdaq-100 closes more than 1.3% higher. Probability is tilted up from the base rate because the Cboe Daily Take reports an after-hours lift.
scenarios.invalidation: Relief gains reverse and VXN and COR1M keep rising.

next_week.confidence_reason: The VIX 25 to 35 regime has wide five-session outcomes (p10 -5.35, p90 6.37). Fed hike risk and the AI debate are unresolved.

scenarios.name: bear
scenarios.text: Rate and AI-spending worries return, with correlation and volatility still rising, and the index falls more than 3% over five sessions.
scenarios.invalidation: VXN and COR1M fall back and the index recovers its 16 to 17 Nov losses.

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.text: Choppy digestion of the Nvidia result, the minutes and the Anthropic debut, with the index inside the band.
scenarios.invalidation: A sharp move in the December hike odds, or a move beyond the band.

scenarios.name: bull
scenarios.text: A relief rebound as AI fears ease and yields stay below their 13 Nov peak, with the index more than 3.5% higher.
scenarios.invalidation: Yields climb back above the 13 Nov level or credit spreads widen further.

next_month.confidence_reason: The December FOMC meeting falls inside the window and the regime history is wide (p10 -8.68, p90 11.92). The same-regime median is positive, so the cuts are asymmetric.

scenarios.text: A hike-driven rise in yields or an AI-spending scare turns the tech correction into a wider drawdown, with the index more than 5% lower.
scenarios.invalidation: A stable rate path and AI earnings that keep beating.

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.text: The index stays within a range as hike pricing is absorbed and the AI trade stabilises.
